source.note: Dirty listing includes untracked files; diff hash includes tracked files only. Binary SHA256 identifies the tested CD executable.

method.topology: same-host loopback, local relays; auto allows direct discovery and fallback, actual telemetry determines route
method.durability: receiver exit measured separately; timed durable completion adds file fsync and directory fsync equally to both tools. Internal tool fsync differences remain part of native completion.
method.verification: SHA256 every output outside all reported transfer timings
method.cache: warm input/page cache, output deleted after SHA256; sync before each trial; no privileged cache dropping
method.limits: No WAN, packet-loss, browser, concurrency or cross-host claims. Directory-tree cases require --input. tmpfs fsync does not represent physical persistence. croc auto telemetry is textual and does not prove direct routing.
method.readiness: readyMs is native invitation-display observation, not equivalent server registration: CD emits its numeric code after live relay/directory admission; upstream croc 11.6.5 prints instructions before local relay setup and remote relay connection. The separate bench-croc-readiness.mjs diagnostic checks pinned source and passive relay logs. No elapsed time is added to croc and the legacy timing fields/gates are unchanged.
method.completionAcceptance: Separately named completionPass1_5/completionPass2 require receiverMs, durableMs and totalMs median speedups of >=1.5 or >=2 against BOTH croc modes in EVERY configured storage/route/payload group, with at least five complete repetitions. They make no invitation-readiness, WAN, concurrency or worldwide claim.
method.admission: CD trial starts spaced at least 0 ms outside timed phases; production code-lookup rate limits remain active
method.transportAccounting: CD counters are encrypted wire bytes, potentially compressed below plaintext size. Full output SHA256/manifest equality proves completion; nonzero valid counters and forced-relay checks prove transport use.

infrastructure.note: --control-dir selects SQLite persistence only for local Wrangler. Direct-runtime controls use separate ephemeral Miniflare state; hosted services use remote state. Disk output remains on --disk-dir for every mode. Compare runtime/control configurations as separate experiments.

worker.compressionObservation: selected compatibility flags are configuration, not negotiated WebSocket extension evidence
worker.note: Separate local runtime configuration control. The explicit Worker bundle bypasses Wrangler, uses ephemeral Miniflare state, and the shared harness adds its frontend HTTP/WebSocket proxy. Do not pool this with Wrangler baselines or call it production throughput.
